newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian airliner missing with 141 on board.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian airliner missing with 141 on board.

text.p: A Nigerian passenger plane went missing on Thursday with 141 people on board, the company operating the aircraft said.
The Aviation Development Company (ADC) said the Boeing 727 had been flying from the southeastern oil city of Port Harcourt to Lagos with 132 passengers and nine crew members.
"A search and rescue operation is going on," said a company statement.
The aircraft had been out of contact with the control tower in Lagos since 5 p.m. (1600 GMT), it said.
A company spokesman said: "We still have no further information. We are expecting the manifest from Port Harcourt."
Airport sources said it was unusual for a plane to be out of touch for so long and it had to be presumed that it must have crashed.
The sources said there were several foreigners on board and that they were probably oil company executives.
Nigeria has had a spate of air disasters in the last few years when the economy has been in trouble and taken a toll on infrastructure.
ADC is 100 percent owned by Nigerian shareholders. It operates domestic services and also flies to some West African countries.
One of its planes crashed in Liberia last year.

In January, a Nigerian presidential aircraft crashed in the north of the country killing the son of military ruler General Sani Abacha. It was followed by another crash in Jos, central Nigeria, in which a state military governor and several other officials were killed.
